problem: Explainable navigation agents (ones that describe their actions) tend to underperform non-explainable ones, and instruction-prediction auxiliary tasks only work with imitation learning because RL has no ground-truth instruction/description data.
motivation: Increasingly complex navigation policies are black boxes, so reliable systems need to verbalize their decisions. The authors observe that action description is compatible with navigation, and that ground-truth descriptions can be produced by a pre-trained description generator (trained on R2R or a VLM), letting RL agents learn to describe actions without hurting, and even improving, navigation.
key_idea: Treat action-description prediction as an auxiliary task in RL/IL navigation, with pseudo ground truth distilled from a pre-trained ADGenerator (video-captioning-like model or VLM) that sees past and/or future observations.
insight: The auxiliary task helps most where the main task is hard and under-constrained (semantic audio-visual navigation, where sound stops), and little on strong VLN baselines. Ablations show ADPredictor pre-training is always important, sharing 2 of 3 decoder layers is best (sharing all 3 hurts, showing a faithfulness-vs-performance trade-off), and past descriptions beat future ones because future prediction is too hard as an auxiliary task. A VLM used zero-shot as ADGenerator still improves over the baseline, but R2R fine-tuned VLM is worse (overfitting).
method: ADGenerator (phase 1): CNN + transformer encoder-decoder (DUET-style graph encoder for VLN) trained on R2R (10,819 train / 1,839 eval) with teacher forcing and cross-entropy to verbalize action/observation sequences (RGBD + semantic images).

ADPredictor: transformer decoder that predicts the description; the goal location/category predictions are fed as the BOS token; shares encoder and most decoder layers with the policy, with task embeddings distinguishing policy vs description.
Joint loss: L_RL + λ L_CE with λ=0.1; ADPredictor is trained with teacher forcing on ADGenerator outputs.
Two-step training: step 1 pre-trains ADPredictor only on ~100k (ObjNav) / 500k (SAVNav) shortest-path episodes labeled by ADGenerator; step 2 trains navigation and description jointly.

P/F/PF-DescRL variants: ADGenerator sees past observations (what was done), future observations along shortest path (what to do), or both; the ADGenerator is used only at training time, and at test time only past observations are available.
VLM ADGenerator: VideoLLaMA2 or Qwen2.5-VL (zero-shot, or QLoRA fine-tuned on R2R) generates descriptions, distilled to ADPredictor via soft targets, removing human-created data.
Applied to SMT (ObjNav), DUET/ScaleVLN (VLN, DAgger IL), SAVi/KSAVEN (SAVNav).

setting.backbone: CNN + transformer policies (SMT, DUET, ScaleVLN, SAVi, KSAVEN) with DescRL ADPredictor, trained from scratch / DD-PPO / DAgger; ADGenerator is CNN+Transformer trained on R2R (or VideoLLaMA2 / Qwen2.5-VL as teachers)
setting.training_data: RL/IL on task datasets; R2R (10,819 instruction-trajectory pairs) to train ADGenerator; ~100k (ObjNav) / 500k (SAVNav) synthetic shortest-path description samples for ADPredictor pre-training; ScaleVLN augmentation data in the VLN ScaleVLN rows
setting.observation: egocentric RGBD (+ binaural audio spectrogram and pose for SAVNav); panoramic views on a nav graph for VLN
setting.action_space: low-level discrete (MoveForward/TurnLeft/TurnRight/Stop) for ObjNav and SAVNav; nav-graph viewpoints for VLN
setting.privileged: none at test time (semantic images and future observations are used only at training by ADGenerator)

numbers.extra: 56/4/7 scene split of 67 MP3D scenes; ADPredictor pre-trained

results: DescRL raises SAVi on semantic audio-visual navigation from SR/SPL 31.6/28.5 (heard) and 24.7/22.4 (unheard) to 37.4/32.4 and 31.4/26.9, beating KSAVEN and other baselines and outperforming other auxiliary tasks. On ObjNav SMT improves from SR 17.9 to 26.7; on VLN gains over DUET/ScaleVLN are marginal but not harmful.
limitations: Dataset bias in ADGenerator descriptions (e.g. hallucinated 'stairs') and lack of object qualifiers, causing stops at the wrong instance of the right category
Domain gap: R2R-trained ADGenerator assumes human-sized robot and a 3 m success radius vs 1 m in SAVNav, leading to premature stops
Gains on strong VLN baselines are small; untested on other RL tasks or EQA
